VI.description: Read the DQMH module-type catalogue by opening DQMH New Module.lvlib\3AGet Module Type Info.vi BY PATH over VI Server and running it. Read-only\3A that VI takes no inputs and only reports.\0A\0AWHY THIS IS A SEPARATE HELPER AND MUST BE RUN FIRST. Script New Module.vi's Module Type terminal is a bare uint16 with NO enum strings in its export\2C so nothing in the pane says what 0 or 1 means. The meaning is a RUNTIME catalogue\3A Type Strings and Descriptions come back as parallel arrays and Module Type indexes them. DQMH 7.x makes module types pluggable\2C so the list differs per station - measured here as Singleton\2C Cloneable\2C Cloneable Panel\2C Singleton Panel\2C where the last two come from an MGI add-on that another machine need not have. An index is therefore only meaningful next to the catalogue it came from\3A read this\2C match the caller's wording to a NAME\2C and take that name's position. Never carry an index between stations or between sessions.\0A\0AWHY BY PATH AND NOT AS A Call. Measured 2026-08-31\3A an AIXML Call naming DQMH New Module.lvlib\3AGet Module Type Info.vi is refused with Error 53\2C Unsupported SubVI\2C because the generator resolves a target by name against what the INSTALLATION can find and the DQMH scripting VIs live under project\5CDelacor\5C - not vi.lib\2C not user.lib\2C not an LVAddon. Open VI Reference takes a PATH and has no such restriction.\0A\0ATHE APPLICATION REFERENCE IS THE IDE'S\2C not the addon's. A generated helper runs inside the AI addon's application instance\2C where the IDE's DQMH VIs do not exist. {LV.Application} -> Project\3AActive Project -> {LV.Project} -> Application yields the IDE's own app reference. A project must therefore be OPEN AND ACTIVE or this answers Error 1055 - which is the commonest reason this helper returns nothing.\0A\0AINDICATORS ARE VARIANTS ON PURPOSE. Ctrl Val.Get hands back a variant\2C and converting it would need a Variant To Data type constant\2C for which the AIXML reference gives two different spellings of the first terminal. A variant indicator needs neither\2C and lvai_run_vi_and_read_values returns compound values as flattened XML in which the type strings are plainly readable.
